extracted.intended_audience: Flipboard users: individual curators, publishers, brands, teams, and creators interested in making or growing Flipboard Magazines
extracted.subtask_description: Guidance and rationale for creating and curating Flipboard Magazines: why to collect stories, how publishers/brands/teams benefit, and how curation improves discovery on the platform.

rubrics_metrics.name: Collect and share stories that shape daily lives
rubrics_metrics.description: It gives people a single place to collect stories that shape their daily lives—and share that inspiration with others.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examples include collecting ideas on healthy living, educating others on cryptocurrency, or presenting a perspective on immigration. Curators provide unique packages around almost any topic. The post points readers to the #MagsWeLove collection as a place to browse exemplary Flipboard Magazines.

rubrics_metrics.name: Publishers should package coverage for events and evergreen topics
rubrics_metrics.description: Publishers can curate stories into packages that cover special events or collect evergreen articles to deliver a full view into a particular area of coverage.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examples: Vanity Fair covering the red carpet at the Oscars; Axios providing perspective on the Russia probe. Guidance emphasizes that magazines let publishers connect with readers who want to go deep, leverage all of their coverage, and build a new type of relationship with Flipboard readers.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use curation to create a quiet, coherent storytelling place (vs social posts)
rubrics_metrics.description: Curation gives people and brands an easy way to bring their passion, expertise or ideas to others—breaking free from the barrage of social posts, people can create a quiet place, filled with information or inspirational ideas that others can sit back and enjoy.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Advice: instead of posting individual items on social channels, curate ideas into a Flipboard Magazine where articles, videos and ideas can be packaged together to truly tell a story. Emphasizes packaging content to tell a narrative rather than atomized social shares.

rubrics_metrics.name: Create collaborative/group magazines for shared conversations
rubrics_metrics.description: If a team or group of friends wants to discuss a topic or share ideas just among their circle, magazines can be made together.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Contrast with sharing via email or Slack, which places articles randomly in someone's stream; a curated magazine is a package anyone on the team can return to at any time. Use cases given: research teams, book clubs. Practical guidance: start curating and then invite contributors.

rubrics_metrics.name: Curation signals the platform to surface better stories
rubrics_metrics.description: Curation is a signal to the platform that brings better stories to everyone.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Flipboard's machine learning team can see what stories are being collected ('flipped') into magazines, how many people are sharing those items, and what types of magazines they are being curated into; the engine can then surface the best stories on any given topic. Encourages curators to provide that signal so Flipboard topics are filled with timely items others find valuable.

rubrics_metrics.name: Collections provide broader perspective and amplify impact
rubrics_metrics.description: Collections of stories can give people a bigger picture, a deeper dive, a more robust perspective on any issue.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The post argues that sometimes hearing the same story from multiple points of view helps advance awareness, and that packaged collections can be more impactful than individual pieces. This is presented as a core rationale for making magazines: to expand perspective and build appreciation for other points of view.
